body:
As a logistics operator, I want to split oversized or incompatible purchase orders into sub-orders so that they can be dispatched across multiple robots when a single robot cannot fulfill the request.

Acceptance Criteria:

– Algorithmically partitioned sub-orders where items are grouped legally by compatibility (e.g., separating refrigerated items from non-refrigerated items if required) and weight/volume constraints.
– Successful multi-robot assignment linking each sub-order to a distinct available robot.
– A structured summary showing the original order, the generated sub-orders, and their respective assigned robots.
title: USEI05

body:
As a logistics operator, I want to evaluate if a single purchase order can be fulfilled by an available robot and assign the most suitable robot based on weight, volume constraints, and highest battery level.

Acceptance Criteria:

– A boolean feasibility result indicating whether any available robot satisfies all constraints (max volume, max weight, and minimum required battery).
– Automatic assignment of the order to the optimal robot (READY status, sufficient capacity, and highest current battery).
– Updated status of the selected robot (e.g., state changed from READY to BUSY) and updated station availability.
title: USEI04

body:
As a Product Owner, I want the relational model to be instantiated in an Oracle SGBD using the SQL DDL code generated by an appropriate tool.

Acceptance Criteria:
– All tables in the database must be populated with data.
– The inserted data should allow verification that the model fulfills the requirements
– It will be shown on Oracle FreeSQL.
title: USBD05

body:
As a logistics operator, I want to manage and filter the queue of pending purchase orders by delivery time windows and customer ID, while keeping orders prioritized by their deadline.

Acceptance Criteria:

– An ordered queue structure that automatically keeps pending orders sorted by their earliest delivery deadline.
– Filtered lists of orders matching specific criteria (e.g., orders due within the next hour or orders belonging to a specific customer ID).
– Functions to query and remove processed orders from the queue safely without breaking collection integrity
title: USEI03

body:
As a Product Owner, I want the relational model to be created (logical level).

Acceptance Criteria:
– The data model should cover the requirements presented in this document, as well as any additional requirements resulting from the provided user stories and feedback/clarifications provided by the client.
– A complete model, including an ER diagram and all constraints, which allows the physical model script for Oracle RDMS to be automatically generated by a specific tool or an LLM.
title: USBD04

body:
As a shopping facility operator, I want to consult the status of parking stations to monitor their total and available capacity, as well as the robots currently parked, including their status and battery levels sorted in  descending order.

Acceptance Criteria:
– A clear status view per station detailing maximum capacity,
occupied spots, and free spots.
– A list of parked robots for a selected station showing theiroperational status (READY, CHARGING, MAINTENANCE) and battery levels.
– Sorted robot outputs driven by custom Comparator implementation (e.g., highest battery level first)
title: USEI02

This is a ”dynamic” document, which should continuously reflect the stakeholders’ shared understanding of the domain.

– The document evolves throughout the semester.
title: USBD01

body:
As an infrastructure planner, I want to import initial information from text/CSV
files (robots, parking stations, and user purchase requests) and load it into the
most appropriate data structures.

Acceptance Criteria:
– Successful parsing and loading of all entities (Robots, Stations, Orders) into Java Collection Framework structures without data loss or corruption.
– Appropriate collection choices based on access patterns.
– Informative error messages or logs for malformed lines or missing values during the import process.
title: USEI01

body:
As a Retailer Administrator, I want to use the back-office application to import the stores and levels of a shopping location from a GeoJSON file, to create the stores available at a shopping location.

Acceptance Criteria:
– The app must import the data from the provided GeoJSON file
– A list of the imported levels and stores must be presented to the user
– The app must insert the imported data into the database
– Importing errors should be clearly displayed
title: USLP06
